Definition: the sky (as aloft; the dual perhaps alluding to the visible arch in which the clouds move, as well as to the higher ether where the celestial bodies revolve)
BiblicalUsage: The God of heaven is Daniel's name for the LORD in a foreign land, and it is the name that answers secrets. Daniel and his fellows desired mercies of the God of heaven concerning the king's dream, and Daniel told the king there is a God in heaven that revealeth secrets. The Son of man came with the clouds of heaven to the Ancient of days, and Nebuchadnezzar ended his madness praising the King of heaven.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the God of heaven rules the kings of earth, and Daniel's whole book is the proof of it. Nebuchadnezzar learned it in the field eating grass, and Belshazzar learned it in a single night. That is why I trust the God of heaven with the affairs of men, because no king rules without His leave.
